Peterson''' (born November 9, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Motor City Cruise]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Rice Owls men's basketball|Rice Owls]] and the [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC Trojans]]. ==Early life and high school career== Peterson grew up in [[Libertyville, Illinois]] and attended [[Libertyville High School]].{{cite web|url=https://basketball.dailyherald.com/sports/20210406/transfer-to-usc-works-out-better-than-expected-for-libertyville-grad-peterson|title=Transfer to USC works out better than expected for Libertyville grad Peterson|work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, Illinois)|Daily Herald]]|date=April 6, 2021|access-date=June 26, 2023}} He was named the [[Lake County, Illinois|Lake County]] Player of the Year as a senior after averaging 26.1 points, 8.5 rebounds, and 4.4 assists per game.{{cite web |last=Huett |first=Wes |date=March 27, 2021 |title=Meet the 12 Illinois high school players as part of the NCAA Tournament's Sweet 16 |url=https://www.pjstar.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2021/03/27/march-madness-illinois-high-school-players-cameron-krutwig/6989177002/ |access-date=June 26, 2023 |work=[[Peoria Journal Star]]}} Peterson committed to playing college basketball for [[Rice Owls men's basketball|Rice]].{{cite web|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2018/4/10/18504365/drew-peterson-8217-s-commitment-to-rice-headlines-recruiting-notebook|title=Drew Peterson’s commitment to Rice headlines recruiting notebook|first=Joe|last=Hendriksen|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|date=April 10, 2018|access-date=June 26, 2023}} ==College career== Peterson began his college career at Rice. He averaged 5 points and 3.3 rebounds per game as a freshman.{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/libertyville/sports/ct-lbr-basketball-drew-peterson-rice-transfer-tl-0409-20200404-ouyt4qcdgbfellh4phm6jedaqq-story.html|title=Libertyville grad Peterson moving on from Rice basketball|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=April 3, 2020|access-date=June 27, 2023}} Peterson played in all 32 of the Owls games, starting all but one, during his sophomore season and averaged 11.1 points, 6.5 rebounds, and 3.5 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://basketball.dailyherald.com/sports/20200516/what-a-rush-x2014-peterson-chooses-usc|title=What a rush -- Peterson chooses USC|work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, Illinois)|Daily Herald]]|date=May 16, 2020|access-date=June 27, 2023}} Following the end of the season, Peterson entered the NCAA transfer portal.{{cite web|url=https://basketball.dailyherald.com/sports/20200401/former-libertyville-star-peterson-is-leaving-rice|title=Former Libertyville star Peterson is leaving Rice|work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, Illinois)|Daily Herald]]|date=April 1, 2020 |access-date=June 26, 2023}} Peterson initially committed to transfer to [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]], but later decommitted and re-opened his recruitment.{{cite web|url=https://www.twincities.com/2020/05/01/on-second-thought-gophers-commit-drew-peterson-reopens-recruitment/|title=Gophers commit Drew Peterson reopens recruitment|work=[[St. Paul Pioneer Press]]|date=May 1, 2020|access-date=June 27, 2023}} He ultimately transferred to [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]].{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/usc/story/2020-05-11/usc-basketball-adds-guard-drew-peterson-a-transfer-from-rice|title=USC adds guard Drew Peterson, a transfer from Rice|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=May 11, 2020|access-date=June 26, 2023}} Peterson averaged 9.8 points, five rebounds, and 2.7 assists per game in his first season with the Trojans.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/usc/Article/USC-basketball-Drew-Peterson-NBA-draft-enters-name-pool-waters-186071327/|title=USC guard Drew Peterson to test NBA draft waters|first=Shotgun|last=Spratling|website=[[247Sports]]|date=April 11, 2022|access-date=June 26, 2023}} As a senior, he was named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12 Conference]] after averaging 12.4 points, 6.2 rebounds, and 3.3 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2022/04/11/uscs-drew-peterson-to-test-nba-draft-waters/|title=USC's Drew Peterson to test NBA Draft waters|work=[[Orange County Register]]|date=April 11, 2022|access-date=June 26, 2023}} Peterson initially entered his name into the [[2022 NBA draft]], but later withdrew and decided to utilize the extra year of eligibility granted to college athletes who played in the 2020 season due to [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and return to USC for a third season.{{cite web|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2022/11/04/usc-basketballs-drew-peterson-back-after-his-one-almost-shining-moment/|title=USC basketball’s Drew Peterson back after his one almost-shining moment|work=[[Orange County Register]]|date=November 4, 2022|access-date=June 26, 2023}} He repeated as a first-team All-Pac-12 selection in his final season after averaging 13.9 points, 6.2 rebounds, and 4.3 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/heats-drew-peterson-lands-with-miami/|title=Heat's Drew Peterson: Lands with Miami|website=[[CBS Sports]]|agency=[[RotoWire]]|date=June 23, 2023|access-date=June 26, 2023}} ==Professional career== ===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Peterson joined the [[Miami Heat]] for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]] and on August 11, 2023, he signed with them.{{cite web|title=HEAT MAKE ROSTER MOVES|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-make-roster-moves|website=NBA.com|date=August 11, 2023|access-date=August 12, 2023}} However, he was waived on October 14.{{cite web|title=HEAT WAIVE PETERSON AND WILLIAMS|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-waive-peterson-and-williams|website=NBA.com|date=October 14, 2023|access-date=October 15, 2023}} On October 30, he joined the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite web|title=Skyforce Announces Training Camp Roster Ahead of 2023-24 Season|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-training-camp-roster-ahead-of-2023-24-season|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=December 14, 2023}} Peterson averaged 15.2 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 4.2 assists in 13 games with the Skyforce.{{cite web|url=https://www.pressherald.com/2023/12/14/sports-digest-messi-mbappe-and-haaland-are-finalists-for-fifa-player-of-the-year-award/|title=Sports Digest: Celtics add Drew Peterson to fill two-way roster opening|work=[[Portland Press Herald]]|date=December 14, 2023|access-date=December 15, 2023}} ===Boston Celtics (2023–2025)=== On December 14, 2023, Peterson signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics Sign Drew Peterson|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/121423-press-release-boston-celtics-sign-drew-peterson|website=NBA.com|date=December 14, 2023|access-date=December 14, 2023}} Nine days later, he made his NBA debut for the Celtics in a 145–108 win over the [[2023–24 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics vs Los Angeles Clippers Box Score|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401585017|website=ESPN.com|date=December 14, 2023|access-date=January 28, 2024}} Peterson became an NBA champion when the Celtics defeated the [[2023–24 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]] in five games in the [[2024 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]]. On July 3, 2024, Peterson re-signed with the Celtics on another two-way contract.{{cite tweet|author=Boston Celtics|title=We have signed Drew Peterson to a two-way contract ☘️|number=1808606713550868823|user=celtics|date=July 3, 2024|access-date=July 3, 2024}} He made 25 appearances (including one start) for Boston during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], posting averages of 2.2 points, 1.6 rebounds, and 0.5 assists.{{Cite web|title=Drew Peterson 2024–25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4397689/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=March 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Charlotte Hornets (2025)=== On July 16, 2025, Peterson signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Drew Peterson To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-sign-drew-peterson-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 16, 2025|access-date=July 16, 2025}} In six appearances for the Hornets, he averaged 0.8 points, 1.5 rebounds, and 0.3 assists.{{Cite web|title=Drew Peterson 2025–26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4397689/drew-peterson|access-date=March 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On December 23, Peterson was waived by Charlotte.{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Waive Drew Peterson|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-waive-drew-peterson|website=NBA.com|date=December 24, 2025|access-date=December 25, 2025}}
